title: The Darwin Incident
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Charlie, a half-human, half-chimpanzee 'humanzee' born after an eco-terrorist group freed his pregnant mother from a testing lab, starts high school at 15 in suburban Missouri and befriends a clever loner, Lucy (Kodansha blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates; SLJ). The Animal Liberation Alliance returns to pull him into its terrorist plot. The series won the Manga Taisho Award in 2022.
life_message: Thinking carefully and caring for others matters more than belonging to any side.

content.note: SLJ: violent 'from the opening pages' and throughout; MangaUpdates Mass Murder/s, Blood and Gore, Serial Killer/s; AniList Terrorism, Gore.
Hunted protagonist and terrorist plots (MangaUpdates; blurb); eco-horror tag (AniList).

Extremist recruitment of a teen (SLJ); animal cruelty tag (MangaUpdates).

folkways.japan: A Japanese author sets the story in the United States, viewing American debates on animal rights and media from outside.

delivery.evidence: SLJ: Charlie's views 'will make readers think'; touches hot-button issues; not called preachy.
delivery.note: The extremist group drives the plot while Charlie weighs its ideas, and the reviewer describes the world as complicated rather than one-sided.

winners_losers: Sympathy lies with Charlie and Lucy; the extremist ALA is the antagonist, though its animal-welfare concern is treated as a real question (to verify).
